title: Talking about food, bodies and results without making promises
audience: Consultants who talk with clients and prospects about food, weight and results, and who write marketing or messages about the service.
learningOutcomes: Explain why a promise of weight loss, a timeline or a guaranteed result must not be made.
Rewrite a claim so that it describes the service honestly and does not promise an outcome.
Describe how to talk about bodies, food and progress without moral labels or body-shaming.
Apply the rules for testimonials, before-and-after images and product recommendations.

instruction.heading: Results are not promised
instruction.body: Weight change, body shape and health outcomes depend on many factors that a consultant cannot control or predict, including the client's health, medication, sleep, stress, activity and circumstances. For that reason this course does not teach you to promise weight loss, to give a timeline, to guarantee a result or to say that a plan will work for everyone. Describe what the service offers, such as general information, habit support and a review of progress against goals the client has chosen, and let the client decide what they want to achieve. The evidence for specific approaches, and the wording of any statement about outcomes, is UNCONFIRMED in this draft and must be checked by the qualified reviewer before it is used.

instruction.heading: Rewriting claims that promise outcomes
instruction.body: Many nutrition claims are written as promises: lose ten kilos in six weeks, melt fat, boost metabolism, detox the body. Do not use those phrases, and do not write a variant of them. Describe the service in terms of what you do and what the client does. For example, say that the service helps clients build habits they choose, and that progress is reviewed together. Avoid words that imply a guaranteed result, a special secret or a shortcut. Consumer and advertising rules may apply to these statements. The applicable rules are UNCONFIRMED in this draft and the reviewer must confirm them before any marketing text is published.

instruction.heading: Talking about bodies and food without judgement
instruction.body: Language about food and bodies can shape how a client feels about themselves. Avoid labels that describe foods as good or bad, clients as good or bad for eating, and bodies as problems to be fixed. Use neutral descriptions, focus on habits the client can practise, and celebrate progress in the terms the client sets. Do not compare a client with another client or with an image. Do not comment on a client's appearance as a way of marking progress. Respect that the client may have a different goal from the one you would suggest.

instruction.heading: Testimonials, before-and-after images and products
instruction.body: A testimonial or a before-and-after image is a claim about results and must be treated as one. Do not use a client's story, photograph or measurements in marketing unless the client has given informed, written consent for that specific use, the image or story has been checked for accuracy, and the reviewer has confirmed that it does not make an outcome claim. Do not recommend, sell or endorse supplements, meal products or other products in this course. If a client asks about a product, refer them to a suitable health professional. The rules that apply to testimonials and product endorsements are UNCONFIRMED in this draft.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor or the reviewer should check every marketing item and standard message template before it is used. A competent practitioner can explain why a promise cannot be made, rewrite an outcome claim into an honest service description, talk about food and bodies without judgement and refuse to use testimonials or product endorsements without the required checks. Escalate any request for a guarantee, any before-and-after use that has not been checked, and any product endorsement request.

procedure: Check the service description and marketing text against the approved wording before it is used.
Remove any promise of a result, timeline, guarantee or secret method.
Describe the service in terms of what is offered and what the client chooses to do.
Use neutral language about food and bodies, and avoid moral labels and comparisons.
Use a testimonial or before-and-after image only with written, specific consent and the required check.
Refer any product question to a suitable health professional, and do not endorse products.

workedExamples.situation: A prospective client asks how many weeks it will take to lose ten kilograms if they follow your programme.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not give a timeline or a figure. Explain that outcomes depend on many factors that you cannot predict, and that the service helps the client build habits and review progress against goals they choose. Suggest they speak with their health professional about a realistic goal if they have a health concern. Do not promise a result to win the client.

workedExamples.situation: A draft social media post says 'Our clients melt fat in just two weeks with our proven method.'
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the draft?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not publish it. The phrases 'melt fat', 'two weeks' and 'proven method' are outcome and evidence claims. Rewrite the post to describe the service without a result, and send the revised text to the reviewer for checking. Confirm that no before-and-after or testimonial is used unless the consent and check have been completed.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved service description and marketing wording
Checklist of prohibited claim types, confirmed by the reviewer
Written consent form for testimonial or image use

commonErrors.error: Promising a weight loss result or timeline to win the client.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the service and the goals the client chooses. Do not give a result or a timeline.

commonErrors.error: Using a before-and-after image in marketing without specific written consent and a check.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not use the image until consent and the reviewer check are complete.

commonErrors.error: Labelling foods or clients as good or bad.
commonErrors.prevention: Use neutral descriptions and focus on habits the client can practise.

commonErrors.error: Recommending a supplement or a meal product because the client asked.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the product question to a suitable health professional and do not endorse products.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Advertising and consumer law may restrict claims about outcomes, evidence and testimonials. The applicable rules are UNCONFIRMED in this draft and must be checked by the reviewer before any marketing is used.
Completing this lesson does not give authority to make clinical claims or to endorse products as health treatments.

qualityStandard: No marketing or message contains a promise of a result, a timeline, a guarantee or a secret method.
Every claim about the service has been checked against the approved wording.
No testimonial or before-and-after image was used without written consent and the required check.
No product was recommended or endorsed in this service.
documentationEvidence: Approved version of each marketing item and standard message template, with the reviewer check recorded.
Written consent for any testimonial or image used.
Record of product questions and the referral made.
summary: Do not promise weight loss, timelines, guarantees or secret methods.
Describe the service in honest terms and let the client choose their goals.
Talk about food and bodies without moral labels or comparisons.
Use testimonials and images only with written consent and a check, and do not endorse products.

knowledgeChecks.question: A prospect asks how fast they will lose weight on your programme. What is the best answer?
options: Give them a timeline of about six weeks so they have a clear goal
Explain that outcomes depend on many factors you cannot predict, and describe what the service offers.
Tell them that most clients lose ten kilograms, without showing any data

knowledgeChecks.question: When may a client's before-and-after image be used in marketing?
options: Whenever the client has been happy with the consult
Only with specific written consent and the required check completed.
Whenever the image shows a visible improvement

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks which supplement will help them lose weight. What is the right response?
options: Name the most popular supplement, since clients usually want a clear answer
Refer the question to a suitable health professional and do not endorse products.
Suggest a supplement that a friend uses, with a note that it works for them

sourceReferences: Catalogue decision NEW-NUT-04 (docs/UPGRADE-PLAN-2026-11-10.md, Phase 2, nutrition row). Written from scratch; there is no source lesson.
Claims, testimonial and advertising rules: UNCONFIRMED. Not checked in this draft. The reviewer must confirm them.
No nutrition outcome, weight-change or product-efficacy claim is made in this lesson. Any such claim must be added only after a source is checked and the reviewer approves it.
